d.d: To separate or scatter (things) as if by sieving.
[with through] To carefully go through a set of objects, or a collection of information, in order to find something.

d.x: The recipe called for sifted flour so it would be fluffier.

d.d: simple past and past participle of sift
A tool for sifting, especially one for powdered cooking ingredients.
Any lamellirostral bird, as a duck or goose, so called because it sifts or strains its food from the water and mud by means of the lamellae of the beak.
present participle and gerund of sift
The act by which something is sifted.
The material which falls through a sieve.
A master or teacher in the context of martial arts, especially kung fu and tai chi.
A spiritual father in esoteric contexts.
